text:
If f : R $\to$ R is a differentiable function and
f(2) = 6,

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{x\to 2}\frac{\int\limits _{6}^{f(x)}2tdt}{(x-2)}$

This is $\frac{0}{0}$ form  so we use L – Hospital Rule.

= $\lim _{x\to 2}\frac{2f(x).f^{'}(x)-0}{1}$

= $2f(2).f^{'}(2)$

= 12f'(2)

Note :  Newton - Leibnitz rule of differentiation under integration

text:
If the system of equations 2x + 3y – z = 0, x + ky
– 2z = 0 and 2x – y + z = 0 has a non-trival solution
(x, y, z), then $\frac{x}{y}+\frac{y}{z}+\frac{z}{x}+k$
is equal to :-
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given 2x + 3y – z = 0, 

x + ky – 2z = 0

2x – y + z = 0

For non trivial solution

$\Delta =0\Rightarrow \left |\begin{array}{lll} 2 & 3 & -1 \\ 1 & k & -2 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \end{array}\right |=0$

$\Rightarrow k=\frac{9}{2}$

$\therefore$ Equations are 2x + 3y – z = 0 ...(i)

2x – y + z = 0 ...(ii)

2x + 9y – 4z = 0 ...(iii)

By (i) – (ii) we get,

4y - 2z = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 2y = z .......(iv)

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{y}{z}=\frac{1}{2}$

From equation (i) and (iv)

2x + 3y - 2y = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 2x + y = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{x}{y}=-\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{x}{y}\times \frac{y}{z}=-\frac{1}{2}\times \frac{1}{2}=-\frac{1}{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{z}{x}=-4$

$\therefore$ $\frac{x}{y}+\frac{y}{z}+\frac{z}{x}+k=\frac{-1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}-4+\frac{9}{2}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot

text:
If the sum and product of the first three terms in
an A.P. are 33 and 1155, respectively, then a value
of its $11^{th}$ term is :-
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the three terms are a - d, a, a + d

Given a - d + a + a + d = 33

$\Rightarrow$ 3a = 33

$\Rightarrow$ a = 11

Also given,

(a - d)a(a + d) = 1155

$\Rightarrow$ $(a^{2} - d^{2})a = 1155$

$\Rightarrow$ $(11^{2} - d^{2})11 = 1155$

$\Rightarrow$ $(11^{2} - d^{2}) = 105$

$\Rightarrow$ d = $\pm$ 4

When d = 4 and a = 11 then series is

7, 11, 15, ....

$\therefore$ $T_{11} = a + 10d = 7 + 10\times$ 4 = 47

When d = -4 and a = 11 then series is

15, 11, 7, ....

$\therefore$ $T_{11} = a + 10d = 15 + 10\times$ -4 = -25
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot

text: The value of the integral $\int\limits _{0}^{1}x\cot ^{-1}(1-x^{2}+x^{4})dx$ is :-
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
I = $\int\limits _{0}^{1}x\cot ^{-1}(1-x^{2}+x^{4})dx$

Let $x^{2} = t$

$\Rightarrow$ 2xdx = dt

At x = 0, t = 0

At x = 1, t = 1

I = $\frac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\cot ^{-1}\left (1-t+t^{2}\right )dt$

= $\frac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{1}{1-t+t^{2}}\right )dt$

= $\frac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{t+(1-t)}{1-t+t^{2}}\right )dt$

= $\frac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{t+(1-t)}{1-t(1-t)}\right )dt$

= $\frac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\left [\tan ^{-1}(1-t)+\tan ^{-1}(t)\right ]dt$

= $\frac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\tan ^{-1}(t)dt+\frac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\tan ^{-1}(1-t)dt$

= $\frac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\tan ^{-1}(t)dt+\frac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\tan ^{-1}(t)dt$

[ As $\frac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\tan ^{-1}(1-t)dt$

= $\frac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\tan ^{-1}[0+1-(1-t)]dt$

= $\frac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\tan ^{-1}(t)dt$ ]

= $2\times \frac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\tan ^{-1}(t)dt$

= $\int\limits _{0}^{1}\tan ^{-1}(t)dt$

Using integration by parts rule

= $\left [t.\tan ^{-1}(t)\right ]_{0}^{1}-\int\limits _{0}^{1}t.\frac{1}{1+t^{2}}dt$

= $\frac{π}{4}-\frac{1}{2}\left [\log \left (1+t^{2}\right )\right ]_{0}^{1}$

= $\frac{π}{4}-\frac{1}{2}\log _{e}2$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot

Let z $\in$ C be such that |z| < 1.

 If $ω=\frac{5+3z}{5(1-z)}$, then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$ω=\frac{5+3z}{5(1-z)}$

$\Rightarrow$ $5ω(1-z)=5+3z$

$\Rightarrow$ $5ω-5ωz=5+3z$

$\Rightarrow$ $5ω-5=5ωz+3z$

$\Rightarrow$ $z(5ω+3)=5(ω-1)$

$\Rightarrow$ $z=\frac{5(ω-1)}{3+5ω}$

$\Rightarrow$ $z=\frac{5(ω-1)}{5\left (ω+\frac{3}{5}\right )}$

$ω=\frac{5+3z}{5(1-z)}$

$\Rightarrow$ $5ω(1-z)=5+3z$

$\Rightarrow$ $5ω-5ωz=5+3z$

$\Rightarrow$ $5ω-5=5ωz+3z$

$\Rightarrow$ $z(5ω+3)=5(ω-1)$

$\Rightarrow$ $z=\frac{5(ω-1)}{3+5ω}$

Given |z|  1

text:
If $\cos x\frac{dy}{dx}-y\sin x=6x$, (0 < x < $\frac{π}{2}$)

and $y\left (\frac{π}{3}\right )$ = 0 then $y\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )$ is equal to :-
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\cos x\frac{dy}{dx}-y\sin x=6x$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{dy}{dx}-y\tan x=6x.\sec x$

This is a linear differential equation.

$\therefore$ I.F = $e^{\int -\tan xdx}$ = $|\cos x|$

As 0 < x < $\frac{π}{2}$, so I.F = $\cos x$

So solution is

y(I.F) = $\int 6x.\sec x(I.F)dx$

$\Rightarrow$ y cosx = $\int 6x.\sec x\cos xdx$

$\Rightarrow$ y cosx = $6\int xdx$

$\Rightarrow$ y cosx $= 3x^{2} + C$

As $y\left (\frac{π}{3}\right )=0$

$\therefore$ $(0)\times \left (\frac{1}{2}\right )=\frac{3π^{2}}{9}+C$

$\Rightarrow C=\frac{-π^{2}}{3}$

$\Rightarrow y\cos x=3x^{2}-\frac{π^{2}}{3}$

For $y\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )$

$y\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\frac{3π^{2}}{36}-\frac{π^{2}}{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\sqrt{3}y}{2}=\frac{-3π^{2}}{12}$

$\Rightarrow y=\frac{-π^{2}}{2\sqrt{3}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot

text:
If the two lines x + (a – 1) y = 1 and
$2x + a^{2}y = 1 (a\in$R – {0, 1}) are perpendicular, then
the distance of their point of intersection from the
origin is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
Line 1 : x + (a – 1) y = 1

Slope of this line $(m_{1}) =$ $\frac{-1}{a-1}$

Line 2 : $2x + a^{2}y = 1$

Slope of this line $(m_{2}) =$ $-\frac{2}{a^{2}}$

Line 1 and Line 2 are perpendicular to each other.

$\therefore$ $m_{1} m_{2} = -1$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left (\frac{-1}{a-1}\right )\left (-\frac{2}{a^{2}}\right )=-1$

$\Rightarrow$ $a^{3}-a^{2}+2=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $(a+1)\left (a^{2}-2a+2\right )$ = 0

$\therefore$ $a=-1$

So lines are

Line 1 : x - 2y - 1 = 0

Line 2 : 2x + y - 1 = 0

Solving these equation we get point of intersection

P$\left (\frac{3}{5},-\frac{1}{5}\right )$

Now distance of P from origin

OP = $\sqrt{\left (\frac{3}{5}\right )^{2}+\left (-\frac{1}{5}\right )^{2}}$

= $\sqrt{\frac{10}{25}}$

= $\sqrt{\frac{2}{5}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot

(in m/min.), at which the level of water is rising
at the instant when the depth of water in the tank
is 10m; is :-
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Given $\frac{dv}{dt}$ $= 5 m^{3}/\min $

 and $θ$ = $\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ tan $θ$ = $\frac{1}{2}$ = $\frac{r}{h}$

$\Rightarrow$ h = 2r

Volume of the cone,

$\Rightarrow$ 5 = $\frac{π}{4}(10)^{2}\frac{dh}{dt}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{dh}{dt}$ = $\frac{1}{5π}$

text:
The vertices B and C of a $\Delta$ABC lie on the line, 

$\frac{x+2}{3}=\frac{y-1}{0}=\frac{z}{4}$ such that BC = 5 units. 

Then the
area (in sq. units) of this triangle, given that the
point A(1, –1, 2), is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

Area of  $\Delta$ABC = $\frac{1}{2}\times BC\times AD$

Given BC = 5 so we need perpendicular
distance of A from line BC.

Let a point D on BC = (3$λ$ - 2, 1, 4$λ$)

Direction ratio of AD

3$λ$ - 3, 2, 4$λ$ - 2

 As AD perpendicular to the BC, so

DR of AD. DR of BC = 0

$(3λ-3)3+2(0)+(4λ-2)4=0$

$9λ-9+16λ-8=0\Rightarrow λ=\frac{17}{25}$

Hence, $D=\left (\frac{1}{25},1,\frac{68}{25}\right )$

$\left |AD–\right |=\sqrt{\left (\frac{1}{25}-1\right )^{2}+(2)^{2}+\left (\frac{68}{25}-2\right )^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \sqrt{\left (\frac{-24}{25}\right )^{2}+4+\left (\frac{18}{25}\right )^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \sqrt{\frac{(24)^{2}+4(25)^{2}+(18)^{2}}{25^{2}}}$

$\Rightarrow \sqrt{\frac{576+2500+324}{25^{2}}}$

$\Rightarrow \sqrt{\frac{3400}{25^{2}}}\Rightarrow \frac{\sqrt{34}.10}{25}=\frac{2\sqrt{34}}{5}$

Area of triangle = $\frac{1}{2}\times \left |BC–\right |\times \left |AD–\right |$

= $\frac{1}{2}\times 5\times \frac{2\sqrt{34}}{5}=\sqrt{34}$

text:
If the function $f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{l} a|π-x|+1,x\leq 5 \\ b|x-π|+3,x>5 \end{array} \right.$

is
continuous at x = 5, then the value of a – b is :-
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
As f(x) is continuous at x = 5 then

$\lim _{x\to 5^{-}}f(x)=f(5)=\lim _{x\to 5^{+}}f(x)$

$\Rightarrow$ $\lim _{h\to 0}f(5-h)=f(5)=\lim _{h\to 0}f(5+h)$

$\Rightarrow$ $\lim _{h\to 0}(a|π-(5-h)|+1)=a|π-5|+1$

 = $\lim _{h\to 0}(b|5+h-π|+3)$

$\Rightarrow$ $a|π-5|+1$ = $a|π-5|+1$

= $b|5-π|+3$

Note : As $π$ = 3.14, then $π$ - 5 = 3.14 - 5 = -1.84 < 0

$\therefore$ $|π-5|$ = - ($π$ - 5) and $|5-π|$ = (5 - $π$)

$\Rightarrow$ $-a(π-5)+1$ = $-a(π-5)+1$ = $b(5-π)+3$

$\Rightarrow$ $-a(π-5)+1$ = $b(5-π)+3$

$\Rightarrow$ $(a-b)(5-π)=2$

$\Rightarrow$ $(a-b)=\frac{2}{(5-π)}$

text:
If $f(x)=[x]-\left [\frac{x}{4}\right ]$ ,x $\in$
4
, where [x] denotes the
greatest integer function, then
options:
Both $\lim _{x\to 4-}f(x)$ and $\lim _{x\to 4+}f(x)$ exist but are not
equal
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=[x]-\left [\frac{x}{4}\right ]$

Here check continuty at x = 4

LHL = $\lim _{x\to 4^{-}}f(x)$

= $\lim _{x\to 4^{-}}[x]-\left [\frac{x}{4}\right ]$

= $\lim _{h\to 0}[4-h]-\left [\frac{4-h}{4}\right ]$

= 3 - 0 = 3

h $\to$ 0 means h > 0 (very small positive value)

So 4 - h = 3.something (means less than 4)

$\therefore$ [4 - h] = [3.something] = 3

and $\left [\frac{4-h}{4}\right ]$ = [0.something] = 0

RHL = $\lim _{x\to 4^{+}}f(x)$

= $\lim _{x\to 4^{+}}[x]-\left [\frac{4}{x}\right ]$

= $\lim _{h\to 0}[4+h]-\left [\frac{4+h}{4}\right ]$

= 4 - 1 = 3

Here [4 + h] = [4.something] = 4

and $\left [\frac{4+h}{4}\right ]$ = [1.something] = 1

And f(4) = $[4]-\left [\frac{4}{4}\right ]$ = 4 - 1 = 3

As LHL = RHL = f(4)

$\therefore$ f is continuous at x = 4.

text:
If m is chosen in the quadratic equation 

$(m^{2} + 1)$
$x^{2} – 3x + (m^{2} + 1)^{2} = 0$ 

such that the sum of its
roots is greatest, then the absolute difference of
the cubes of its roots is :-
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given quadratic equation 

$(m^{2} + 1)$
$x^{2} – 3x + (m^{2} + 1)^{2} = 0$

Let roots of the equation $α$ and $β$.

$\therefore$ Sum of roots = $α$ + $β$ = $\frac{3}{m^{2}+1}$

Product of roots = $αβ$ $= m^{2} + 1$

$\frac{3}{m^{2}+1}$ is maximum when m = 0

Hence equation becomes $x^{2} – 3x + 1 = 0$

$α+β=3$,    $αβ=1$    

$|α-β|$ = $\sqrt{(α+β)^{2}-4αβ}$ = $\sqrt{(3)^{2}-4.1}$ = $\sqrt{5}$

$\left |α^{3}-β^{3}\right |=\left |(α-β)(α^{2}+β^{2}+αβ)\right |$

= $\sqrt{5}\left |(α+β)^{2}-αβ\right |$

$=\sqrt{5}(9-1)=8\sqrt{5}$

text:
Two newspapers A and B are published in a city.
It is known that 25% of the city populations reads
A and 20% reads B while 8% reads both A and
B. Further, 30% of those who read A but not B
look into advertisements and 40% of those who
read B but not A also look into advertisements,
while 50% of those who read both A and B look
into advertisements. Then the percentage of the
population who look into advertisement is :-
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

The total population to be 100 (for simplicity's sake) and the percentages can be treated as actual numbers of people in this context.

The percentage of people who read newspaper A is given as 25. However, among these, there are people who read both newspapers A and B, given as 8. To find the number of people who read only newspaper A, we subtract the number of people who read both from the total number of people who read A. That is,

n(A only) = 25 – 8 = 17

Similarly, the number of people who read only newspaper B is calculated as :

n(B only) = 20 – 8 = 12

Now, we are given the percentage of each of these groups that look into the advertisements:

30% of those who read A but not B,
40% of those who read B but not A,
50% of those who read both A and B.

To find the total percentage of the population that looks into advertisements, we add up the contributions from each of these groups. We calculate each group's contribution by multiplying the size of the group by the percentage of that group that looks at advertisements :

= $\frac{30}{100}\times 17$ (from A only) + $\frac{40}{100}\times 12$(from B only) + $\frac{50}{100}\times 8$(from both A and B)

= 5.1 (from A only) + 4.8 (from B only) + 4 (from both A and B)

Adding these up, we get

= 13.9

This means that 13.9% of the total population looks into the advertisements.

So, the correct answer is :

Option D : 13.9.

$\Rightarrow$ x = 36

Also given mean = 42

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{10+22+26+29+34+x+42+67+70+y}{10}$ = 42

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{300+x+y}{10}$ = 42

$\Rightarrow$ 300 + x + y = 420

$\Rightarrow$ 336 + y = 420

$\Rightarrow$ y = 84

$\therefore$ $\frac{y}{x}=\frac{84}{36}$ = $\frac{7}{3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot

text:
The area (in sq. units) of the region

A = {(x, y) : $\frac{y{}^{2}}{2}$ $\leq$ x $\leq$ y + 4} is :-
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$y^{2} = 2x ...........(1)$

and x = y + 4 .............(2)

Solving (1) and (2)

$(x - 4)^{2} = 2x$

$\Rightarrow$ $x^{2} - 10x + 16 = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ x = 8, 2 and y = 4, -2

Integrating in y direction from A to B

Required area (A) = $\int\limits _{-2}^{4}\left (y+4-\frac{y^{2}}{2}\right )dy$

= $\left [\frac{y^{2}}{2}+4y-\frac{y^{3}}{6}\right ]_{-2}^{4}$

= $\left (\frac{16}{2}+16-\frac{64}{6}\right )$ - $\left (\frac{4}{2}-8+\frac{8}{6}\right )$

= 30 - 12 sq. unit

= 18 sq. unit

text:
If a unit vector $\vec{a}$ makes angles $π$/3 with $\hat{i}$ , $π$/ 4
with $\hat{j}$ and $θ\in$(0, $π$) with $\widehat{k}$, then a value of $θ$
is :-
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A unit vector $\vec{a}$ makes angles $π$/3 with $\hat{i}$

$\therefore$ $α$ = $π$/3

 and $π$/ 4
with $\hat{j}$ 

$\therefore$ $β$ = $π$/ 4

and $θ\in$(0, $π$) with $\widehat{k}$

$\therefore$ $γ$ = $θ$

We also know,

$\cos ^{2}α+\cos ^{2}β+\cos ^{2}γ$ = 1

$\Rightarrow$ $\cos ^{2}\frac{π}{3}+\cos ^{2}\frac{π}{4}+\cos ^{2}θ$ = 1

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2}+\cos ^{2}θ$ = 1

$\Rightarrow$ $\cos ^{2}θ$ = $\frac{1}{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\cos θ$ = $\pm \frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $θ$ = $\frac{π}{3}$ or $\frac{2π}{3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot

text:
A rectangle is inscribed in a circle with a diameter
lying along the line 3y = x + 7. If the two adjacent
vertices of the rectangle are (–8, 5) and (6, 5), then
the area of the rectangle (in sq. units) is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Distance between point A and B is  = 14 unit

As y coordinate of point A(-8, 5) and B(6, 5) are same. So line AB is parallel to the x axis. 

Point O is the center of the circle and OP is the perpendicular to the line AB. And P is the mid point of line AB.

$\therefore$ Point P = $\left (\frac{-8+6}{2},\frac{5+5}{2}\right )$ = (-1, 5)

As OP is perpendicular to the line AB and AB is parallel to the x axis then OP is parallel to the y axis. So x coordinate of line OP is constant.

$\therefore$ x coordinate of O  = -1

And point O lies on the line 3y = x + 7

$\therefore$ 3y = -1 + 7

$\Rightarrow$ y = 2

$\therefore$ Center O = (-1, 2)

$\therefore$ OP = 3

Then BC = 2OP = 6

$\therefore$ Area of rectangle = (AB)(BC)

= 14 $\times$ 6

= 84
